Honestly, it might. Here's why:

- The AI editor doesn't put a layer on top of your clip. It makes the whole video again from your clip plus my instruction. So faces, motion, colors and small details can shift a little, even when I tell it to keep everything else the same.
- Small text is hard for it. "@flightschool" might come out with wrong or wobbly letters, and it may not stay see-through or in the same spot from frame to frame.
- On the free plan the result is also 480p, so if your clip is sharper than that, it will look softer.

If you need the clip to stay exactly the same, use a normal editor instead. It only takes a minute:
- **CapCut / iMovie / Premiere:** add a text layer that says "@flightschool", make it small, put it in the bottom-right corner and set opacity to about 40–50%.
- **ffmpeg (free, command line):**
  `ffmpeg -i radio-lines.mp4 -vf "drawtext=text='@flightschool':fontcolor=white@0.5:fontsize=h/25:x=w-tw-20:y=h-th-20" -c:a copy radio-lines-watermarked.mp4`

I can still try the AI version if you want to see how it turns out. It uses credits, and I can't promise it will leave the rest of the clip alone. Should I go ahead, or will you use one of the options above?
